body.statement:
There exists a well-typed explicit instance \(I\) in the declared single-cycle sparse-source class, with one induced chordless directed two-cycle and three independent binary private sources, for which the uniform identification condition
\[
 H(\theta)K(\theta')=H(\theta')K(\theta)
 \quad\text{for all }\theta,\theta'\in\mathcal F_+(p)
\]
holds at every \(p\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{feas}}\) having \(\mathcal F_+(p)\ne\varnothing\), but no rational arithmetic circuit \(C\) in the supplied regime probabilities represents \(H/K\) on the full positive feasible image.  For this instance \(\mathsf{SC\mbox{-}CTFID}(I)\) terminates and returns the obstruction \(O\).  Hence the implication from uniform identification to a rational-circuit output, and consequently the assertion that \(O\) is never returned, are false for the stated input class and output language.
body.justification: This is the desired cyclic formula-or-verifiable-same-class-countermodel theorem, but it remains open at rational descent and universal boundary transmission; the closed termination and output-validity claims are stated separately.
body.gap: Acyclic CTFID completeness does not imply that a positive-real sparse-source fiber-constant ratio descends to one rational circuit, nor that every local cyclic separator survives arbitrary stored exterior interfaces.
body.consumer: cfid obtains safe formula and certificate feedback from the proved output-soundness theorem, while unconditional formula-or-certificate completeness awaits the two isolated obligations.
body.proof_tex:
Let the endogenous variables be \(V=\{W,Y\}\), with alphabets
\[
 \mathcal X_W=\{0,1,2,3\},\qquad \mathcal X_Y=\{0,1\},
\]
and let \(G\) have precisely the directed edges \(W\to Y\) and \(Y\to W\).  Thus its only nontrivial directed strongly connected component is the induced chordless directed two-cycle \(W\to Y\to W\).  There are no bidirected edges.  Consequently the equivalence relation generated by directed-SCC membership and bidirected adjacency has one class, and that class contains exactly this one original cycle.  This verifies \(\text{ass:chordless-cycle-scc}\) and \(\text{ass:one-cycle-per-district}\).

Take three binary primitive sources \(S=\{s_1,s_2,s_3\}\), write their states as \(U_1,U_2,U_3\in\{0,1\}\), and set
\[
 \operatorname{inc}(s_i)=\{Y\},\qquad i=1,2,3.
\]
Give them the product law required by \(\text{ass:source-independence}\), and abbreviate
\[
 x=P(U_1=1),\qquad y=P(U_2=1),\qquad z=P(U_3=1).
\]
Every source has one child, so \(1\leq |\operatorname{inc}(s_i)|\leq2\), as required by \(\text{ass:sparse-source-incidence}\).  Define the structural equations, with multiplication denoting Boolean conjunction, by
\[
 W=0,
 \qquad
 Y=\begin{cases}
 U_1U_2,&W=0,\\
 U_1U_3,&W=1,\\
 U_2U_3,&W=2,\\
 U_1,&W=3.
 \end{cases}
\]
Although the graph permits \(Y\) as a parent of \(W\), the equation for \(W\) is allowed to ignore that argument because \(\text{def:model-class}\) requires the functional graph only to be bounded by \(G\).

For each fixed source tuple, the equations have a unique solution after every endogenous-subset intervention and every boundary assignment.  If both equations are retained, the first equation gives \(W=0\) and the second then gives the unique value \(Y=U_1U_2\).  If only the equation for \(W\) is retained, its unique solution is \(W=0\), irrespective of the boundary value of \(Y\).  If only the equation for \(Y\) is retained, its boundary value of \(W\) selects exactly one of the four displayed Boolean values.  If neither equation is retained, uniqueness is vacuous.  These four cases exhaust the subsets of \(V\).  Hence \(\text{ass:subset-unique-solvability}\) holds without an exceptional source set, and every decoded response profile lies in \(\mathcal L\) by \(\text{def:legal-profiles}\).  Taking \(\Omega_{s_i}=\{0,1\}\) with the displayed decoder therefore gives an explicit legal product-simplex parameter space
\[
 \Theta_{\mathcal L}=[0,1]^3.
\]
All decoder and probability-table entries have coefficients in \(\{0,1\}\), so the resulting instance \(I\) is well typed in the sense of the frozen input definition.

Use the complete regime menu
\[
 \mathcal R=\bigl\{r_0=(\varnothing,\varnothing),\ r_1=(\{W\},1),\ r_2=(\{W\},2)\bigr\}.
\]
Put
\[
 a=xy,\qquad b=xz,\qquad c=yz.
\]
Under \(r_0\), the only nonzero cells have \(W=0\), and
\[
 P(W=0,Y=1)=a,qquad P(W=0,Y=0)=1-a.
\]
Under \(r_1\) and \(r_2\), respectively,
\[
 P(Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(W=1))=b,qquad
 P(Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(W=2))=c,
\]
with complementary zero cells \(1-b\) and \(1-c\).  Thus every coordinate of \(p=\Phi(\theta)\) belongs to \(\mathbb Q[a,b,c]\), while \(a,b,c\) themselves are coordinates of the three complete laws.

Let
\[
 A=\{Y_{\operatorname{do}(W=3)}=1\},
 \qquad
 B=\{Y_{\operatorname{do}(W=2)}=1\}.
\]
These are unnested counterfactual events.  The structural equations give
\[
 A=\{U_1=1\},qquad B=\{U_2=1,U_3=1\},
\]
and source independence therefore gives the exact target polynomials
\[
 H(x,y,z)=xyz,qquad K(x,y,z)=yz=c.
\]
Whenever \(K>0\), division is legitimate and
\[
 q=\frac{H}{K}=x.
\]

We next prove the frozen uniform identification condition.  Let \(\theta=(x,y,z)\) and \(\theta'=(x',y',z')\) belong to the same positive fiber \(\mathcal F_+(p)\).  Equality of their complete menu laws gives
\[
 xy=x'y'=a,qquad xz=x'z'=b,qquad yz=y'z'=c,
\]
and positivity of the denominator gives \(c>0\).  Consequently
\[
 x^2=\frac{(xy)(xz)}{yz}=\frac{ab}{c}
      =\frac{(x'y')(x'z')}{y'z'}=(x')^2.
\]
Both \(x\) and \(x'\) are source probabilities and hence nonnegative, so \(x=x'\).  Since \(H=xK\) and \(H'=x'K'\), while equality of \(p\) gives \(K=K'=c\), it follows that
\[
 H(\theta)K(\theta')=x c^2=x'c^2=H(\theta')K(\theta).
\]
This argument also covers \(x=0\); the only division was by the explicitly positive quantity \(c=K\).  Thus the ratio is constant on every positive source-realizable fiber.

It remains to prove that the identified ratio has no rational-circuit representation.  Suppose to the contrary that a circuit \(C\) as defined in the frozen core represents the ratio on the full positive feasible image.  After substituting the displayed complete-law coordinates, all constants and complementary cells, that circuit becomes a rational function \(R(a,b,c)\in\mathbb Q(a,b,c)\).  Its verified divisor is nonzero on every image point with \(c>0\).  In particular, for every \((x,y,z)\in(0,1)^3\),
\[
 R(xy,xz,yz)=x. \tag{1}
\]
Write \(R=P/Q\) with \(P,Q\in\mathbb Q[a,b,c]\) and \(Q\ne0\).  Cross-multiplying (1) is valid on this open cube and gives
\[
 P(xy,xz,yz)-xQ(xy,xz,yz)=0.
\]
A polynomial over \(\mathbb Q\) that vanishes on an open box is the zero polynomial: fixing all but one coordinate gives a univariate polynomial with infinitely many roots, and induction over the three coordinates proves the assertion.  Hence (1) holds as an identity in \(\mathbb Q(x,y,z)\).

The substitution \(a\mapsto xy\), \(b\mapsto xz\), \(c\mapsto yz\) embeds \(\mathbb Q(a,b,c)\) into \(\mathbb Q(x,y,z)\).  Indeed, distinct monomials remain distinct: the exponent triple of
\[
 (xy)^i(xz)^j(yz)^k
\]
is \((i+j,i+k,j+k)\), from which \((i,j,k)\) is recovered by
\[
 i=\frac{(i+j)+(i+k)-(j+k)}2,quad
 j=\frac{(i+j)+(j+k)-(i+k)}2,quad
 k=\frac{(i+k)+(j+k)-(i+j)}2.
\]
Now consider the field automorphism
\[
 \sigma:\mathbb Q(x,y,z)\longrightarrow\mathbb Q(x,y,z),
 \qquad \sigma(x,y,z)=(-x,-y,-z).
\]
It fixes \(xy,xz,yz\), and therefore fixes every element of the embedded field \(\mathbb Q(a,b,c)\).  The rational identity (1) would place \(x\) in that fixed field.  Applying \(\sigma\) would then give simultaneously
\[
 \sigma(x)=x
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 \sigma(x)=-x,
\]
which is impossible in characteristic zero.  This contradiction proves that no such rational circuit \(C\) exists.  Equivalently, on the strictly positive part of the image the identified value is the positive algebraic branch
\[
 q=x=\sqrt{\frac{ab}{c}},
\]
and the sign branch excluded by probability positivity is precisely what prevents rational descent.

Finally, apply \(\text{thm:sc-ctfid-output-soundness}\) to this well-typed instance.  The algorithm terminates.  Validation cannot return \(\mathsf{invalid}\), because the graph, alphabets, source arities, legal bits, decoder, and the recomputed \(\Phi,H,K\) have just been verified.  A circuit output is impossible by the preceding nonrationality proof.  A verifier-accepted negative certificate is also impossible: by \(\text{def:negative-certificate}\) and \(\text{def:certificate-verifier}\) it would supply two legal positive-denominator source-mass vectors with the same \(p\) and a nonzero target cross-product, contradicting the uniform equality proved above.  The final-output clause of \(\text{def:algorithm-handle}\) leaves only \(O\).  Therefore \(\mathsf{SC\mbox{-}CTFID}(I)\) returns \(O\), refuting both disputed clauses of the original target.
